IonQ Jumped 7%, Rigetti Up 8% on Intel's $2.3 Billion Quantum Buy: "Full-Stack Quantum Computing Business" ©vkstudio via Canva
Key Takeaways

IonQ shares rose 7% today, Rigetti rose 8% and D-Wave rose about 4%, after Intel agreed to buy quantum software company Classiq in a deal reportedly worth about $2.3 billion.

A major chipmaker paying that much for quantum software is a vote of confidence in the sector, and IonQ's selloff over the past month looks overdone.

IonQ fell 24% in a month amid a broader quantum selloff and worries about new shares, and its share count has nearly doubled since the end of 2024.

IonQ reports third-quarter results on Nov. 5, its first quarter with SkyWater included, and Wall Street expects 254% revenue growth.

IonQ (IONQ:NYSE) is up 7% today after Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) agreed to buy quantum software company Classiq, a deal Bloomberg reported is worth about $2.3 billion. The rest of the group came along for the ride: Rigetti Computing (RGTI:NASDAQ) rose 8%, and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS:NASDAQ) gained about 4%.

Intel announced the deal after Monday's close and didn't give a price. In its announcement, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Classiq "transforms Intel's Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business."

Intel Just Put a Price on Quantum Software

That's a big check for software alone. And Classiq's code runs on all kinds of quantum hardware, including trapped-ion machines like the ones IonQ builds.

The timing helps IonQ, too. The stock had dropped 24% in a month as quantum stocks sold off broadly and investors worried about dilution from its $2 billion stock sale and its all-stock Elisity deal, worth up to $1.3 billion.

The dilution is real. IonQ's diluted share count roughly doubled from 2021 to 2025:

IONQ Diluted Shares Outstanding: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

And 429 million shares were outstanding as of Oct. 23, before a single Elisity share has been issued.

IonQ Stock Looks Cheap Against Its Own History

IonQ ended Monday at 19x forward sales. Its three-year average is 75x, and it peaked at 215x in October 2025:

IONQ Stock NTM P/S: 2023-2026 (TIKR)

Part of that drop is the revenue mix, though. Forward sales now include SkyWater's foundry revenue, which BofA valued at just 2x sales in September.

TIKR Tracks 14 Analysts on IonQ. How Many Say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on IonQ, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See IonQ's Analyst Ratings

Intel Wants What IonQ Already Has

IonQ calls itself "the world's leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry." Now Intel is building the same thing, with far deeper pockets. That's a vote for IonQ's strategy, even if Intel's deal won't close until the first half of 2027.

title: Intel, Oracle, IBM Join Objections to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue, Bringing Total to 26

Intel, Oracle, IBM Join Objections to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue, Bringing Total to 26

The tech sector's resistance to tokenized stocks keeps building.

Intel, Oracle, IBM, and quantum computing firm IonQ are the latest companies to object to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice from the venue dated Monday.

Myriad: Which company will IPO next? Click to make your prediction.

The planned platform, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, now lists 26 objecting issuers.

That's up from 22 in its Oct. 23 notice, which added Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Marvell. The tally stood at 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15, when the first batch included Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group. In less than two weeks, the list has nearly tripled.

Technology companies dominate the roster. Microsoft, Alphabet, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Arm, Cisco, and now Intel and Oracle have all objected, along with banks Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo.

IBM and IonQ add two quantum computing players. As before, the notices don't explain the companies' reasons or what an objection means for whether a stock can trade on the platform.

OKXICE TSV plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

Users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable "soulbound" token to trade. The venue is set to operate under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.

The latest notice highlights a key risk for investors. Each token represents a claim on a real share held by a third-party "tokenizer" through a registered broker-dealer. If that broker-dealer failed, the notice says, it's uncertain whether tokenized shares in a self-custodied wallet would count as customer property or be covered by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, which protects brokerage customers when firms fail.

Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks

The notice also says trades must be fully funded, with no margin or borrowing. Liquidity providers don't have to be registered market makers and can pull their liquidity at any time.

OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling plans for the venue this month.

title: Intel faces test of recovery as Wedbush looks beyond Q3 results
detail:
Intel faces test of recovery as Wedbush looks beyond Q3 results
Proactive
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 10:34 AM MST 2 min read
INTC
INL
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Intel faces test of recovery as Wedbush looks beyond Q3 results Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) is expected to beat third-quarter revenue and earnings forecasts, according to Wedbush, but the broker said the chipmaker's fourth-quarter outlook and guidance on 2027 growth and capital spending will be more important in determining how its shares perform.

The broker maintained its 'neutral' rating and $98 price target, saying Intel's shares had fallen about 32% over the past month, creating a more balanced investment outlook.

Wedbush expects third-quarter revenue of $16.3 billion, in line with Intel's guidance midpoint and broadly matching analysts' consensus, with non-GAAP earnings of $0.38 a share and gross margins of 42%.

The broker said improving server supply late in the quarter could support results, although weaker personal computer demand and rising memory and substrate costs could limit the scale of any earnings beat.

Research firm IDC estimated that PC shipments fell about 20% year on year and 9% sequentially during the quarter, creating pressure on Intel's client computing business.

Wedbush forecasts fourth-quarter revenue of $17.5 billion, up 7% sequentially, compared with the $16.9 billion consensus estimate, while projecting earnings of $0.49 a share against analysts' forecast of $0.43.

The broker expects gross margins to improve to 44% in the fourth quarter as a shift towards server products supports profitability, making management's guidance a key focus for investors.

Wedbush also highlighted the potential impact of Intel's August equity issuance, which raised capital through about 242 million shares at $95 each, increasing its estimated weighted share count by about 2% in the third quarter and 5% in the fourth.

The broker said investors would look for additional guidance on 2027 expectations, including capital expenditure, as they assess whether Intel's recovery can be sustained.

Wedbush's $98 price target is based on about 45 times its forecast 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 a share, less estimated net debt of $2.37 a share.

Factors Likely to Have Influenced CTSH Q3 Performance

Cognizant is expected to have benefited from strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-led transformation, continued momentum in Financial Services, the ramp-up of large deals and incremental revenues from acquisitions in the third quarter of 2026. Growing adoption of AI-powered software engineering, cloud modernization, cybersecurity and business process services is likely to have supported performance.

Financial Services is expected to have remained Cognizant's strongest growth engine, benefiting from robust demand across banking, capital markets and insurance. In the second quarter, Financial Services revenues increased 12% year over year to $1.73 billion, marking the second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. This momentum is likely to have continued into the third quarter, supported by modernization projects, growing demand for AI-enabled operations and increased adoption of outcome-based solutions.

Cognizant's healthy large-deal pipeline and the conversion of previously secured contracts into revenues are expected to have supported third-quarter results. The company signed seven large deals, each exceeding $100 million in total contract value, during the second quarter, including three new client relationships. Trailing 12-month bookings increased 5% year over year to $29.1 billion, representing a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1.3.

Increasing enterprise adoption of generative AI, agentic AI and automation is likely to have driven demand for Cognizant's AI engineering, digital transformation and managed services offerings. The company reported more than 8,000 AI engagements in the second quarter, with more than 40% of its software development work becoming AI-assisted. Its Cognizant AI Delivery Operating System, Neuro AI platforms and context engineering capabilities are helping enterprises modernize legacy systems, automate workflows and improve operational efficiency.

Expanding alliances with Google Cloud, Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft and ServiceNow are also likely to have strengthened Cognizant's competitive positioning and supported new business opportunities. Cognizant's acquisitions of Astreya and 3Cloud are expected to have supported third-quarter revenues.

title: Can Marvell Stock Jump 30%?
detail:
Can Marvell Stock Jump 30%?
Trefis Team

Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Marvell Technology (MRVL) returned 182.9% over the twelve months to October 26, 2026, compared with 15.3% for the S&P 500. Another 30% rise from that close would require a bet that Marvell's data center chip sales keep growing the way they did over that year. Even with such an increase, the stock would remain short of its June 4, 2026 close, which sat 35.3% above the October 26 close. Could you have seen that data center growth coming before October 2025?

What Marvell Said And Filed Before October 2025

Yes, and management said as much before the figures showed it. On the December 3, 2024 earnings call, management said Marvell had "rapidly transformed into an AI-first data center semiconductor company." Financial results for that quarter, which ended November 2, 2024, remained weak: sales rose only 6.9% from a year earlier, and the company posted an operating loss. So the earliest sign was a claim you had to take on trust.

Earnings calls and subsequent filings began to show the shift throughout 2025. On the March 5, 2025 call, management said custom AI silicon programs were moving into full-scale production. In the quarter ended May 3, 2025, with results filed on May 30, sales grew 63.3% from a year earlier. By the quarter ended August 2, 2025, Marvell earned an operating margin of 14.9%, compared with an operating loss in the same quarter the previous year. On the August 28, 2025 call, management said data center sales now made up three-quarters of revenue.

None of this was hidden, and the stock had already started moving. Shares climbed 44.6% in the six months before October 23, 2025, when the twelve months measured here began.

How Much Bigger Marvell's Data Center Business Got

Data center sales reached $2.17 billion in the quarter ended August 1, 2026, up 46% from a year earlier. This accounted for 79% of Marvell's revenue, compared with about three quarters a year before. The mix barely changed: the business that already made up most of Marvell kept growing. Not every chip stock climbed the way Marvell did. Broadcom fell 3.7%, and NVIDIA rose 18.9% over the same twelve months. Advanced Micro Devices came closest of the three, with a 126.1% return.

Investors also pay much more for each dollar of Marvell's total sales. At the October 26, 2026 close, shares traded at 22.2 times sales over the last four quarters, compared with 9.2 times at the end of June 2025.

Intel Corporation INTC is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 earnings after the closing bell on Oct. 29. In the to-be-reported quarter, the company is likely to have recorded slightly higher revenues from the Client Computing Group (CCG) segment despite high customer inventory levels and a conservative approach toward placing orders for high-value items.

Factors at Play

CCG is the company's largest segment and accounts for the lion's share of total revenues. It includes computer CPUs, several server boards, form factor systems and graphic products.

During the quarter, Intel expanded its multi-year collaboration with Alphabet Inc.'s Google Cloud. The partnership will help Intel integrate generative AI and cloud technologies across its global operations to support innovation and business growth. Under the agreement, Intel will deploy Gemini Enterprise across its workforce, enabling employees to automate tasks and enhance workflows across engineering, supply chain and corporate operations. Through this collaboration, Intel aims to strengthen its position in AI-driven enterprise and semiconductor innovation. The company will also utilize the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to create custom AI tools for different business functions. In addition, Intel is exploring AI solutions to improve marketing and communications by generating targeted content, identifying relevant subject-matter experts and preparing executive materials more efficiently. These developments are likely to have supported the CCG segment's top line during the quarter.

Intel also extended its Core Ultra platform to new Googlebook laptops powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors. The latest processors deliver responsive performance and power efficiency for modern computing. Built on Intel's advanced 18A process technology, the Core Ultra Series 3 integrates CPU, GPU and NPU architectures to support demanding workloads and AI-enabled experiences. The platform is designed to help users multitask across applications while maintaining efficient power consumption for longer battery life. The company has also added enhanced connectivity features to the new Googlebook laptops, including Intel Wi-Fi 7, Dual Intel Bluetooth 6.0 and Intel Thunderbolt. These technologies deliver fast and reliable connections across different environments while supporting seamless device experiences.

However, Intel has been facing challenges due to the disruptive rise of over-the-top service providers in this dynamic industry. Price-sensitive competition for customer retention in the core business is expected to intensify in the coming days. Aggressive competition is likely to limit the ability to attract and retain customers and affect operating and financial results.

Moreover, high raw material prices due to Middle East tensions, the prolonged Russia-Ukraine war and the consequent economic sanctions against the Putin regime have affected the operation schedules of various firms, affecting Intel's demand schedule. High technological obsolescence of most products has further escalated operating costs.
